column1: # gate-ledger.tsv — every gate fire observed in dispatch rehearsal iterations 01–16
# (and the 05b same-intent rerun), labelled. Change seam-gate-safety, slice G3.
# Data only: nothing reads this file to decide a gate. gate-ledger-summary.sh
# counts it; test-planner-gate-ledger.sh checks it.
# Sources: the rehearsal's findings.md, iter-*/run-record.md (Blocks tables) and
# block-audit.md, with deep-dive D's corrections: RESOLUTION_NOT_PROPAGATED (F25)
# is false, not true; UNSTATED_DEPENDENCY (F43) is debatable, not true.
# Iterations 12–16 (rows added for delivery-first M3): the final column of each
# run record's reconciled G7 review table, else its Blocks table; iterations 14
# and 16 halted before a review, so their unreviewed fires are debatable/
# unlabelled unless a finding settles them (F40, F89, F94).
# One row per fire, or per group of identical fires (same iteration, gate, round,
# code, unit and label: see count). Aggregate halt codes (DRAFT_NOT_READY,
# CROSSCHECK_BLOCKED, DEMOTE_CEILING) are not rows: the fires under them are.
# Audit advisories and MISSED entries that never blocked are not rows.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   iter      01..16 or 05b
#   gate      crosscheck | draft | draft-crosscheck (Crosscheck re-run inside the
#             draft gate's loop) | draft-guard (a revise guard) | refinement |
#             dor-check (the per-iteration negative control)
#   round     draft-gate evaluation round that raised the fire (0 = first scan;
#             a run-record "Round N" revise row is evaluation round N-1);
#             a-b when it stood from round a to b; for draft-guard and
#             draft-crosscheck rows, the revise round they judged; Refinement
#             round; - otherwise
#   code      the gate code
#   class     what the gate did at the time: block | warn | revert
#   outcome   halted | revised | rebutted | demoted (round limit) | reverted |
#             accepted | hand-fixed (an operator answer or a mid-run fix) |
#             logged (warn) | expected (negative control)
#   unit      spec slug; a file name; (cross-file); (multiple); negative-control;
#             #N = the Nth ticket TicketGen created, when the spec set was not kept
#   count     number of identical fires in this row
#   label     true (a real plan gap) | false (the check was wrong, or its cause
#             was a bug elsewhere) | debatable (people could disagree, or no label
#             was recorded at run time: cause unlabelled)
#   cause     plan-gap | live-logic (the check's own logic, as it still is) |
#             checker-bug | upstream-bug (a prompt or generator bug fed the check
#             bad input) | format (model output broke a strict format) | env
#             (sandbox) | negative-control | unlabelled
#   fixed     yes | partial | no | - (true rows)
#   live      false rows: yes when what made the false fire is still on main
#             today (the same output would fire the same way and nothing on main
#             prevents it), no when a fix on main removed it. - for other rows
#   f_id      rehearsal finding id(s), space-separated, or -
#   evidence  <file>:<line> under the rehearsal folder (findings.md or
#             iter-NN/run-record.md). That line names the f_id, else the code;
#             unlabelled rows point at the run's summary line
#   note      what fired and why (no tracker ids, initiative ids, names or paths)
# G4 rule (seam-audit PLAN): only a false fire with live=yes counts toward a
# demotion. Fires from checker bugs already fixed (F12/F24, F22, F33, F52, F67)
# do not count, and a DEPENDENCY_CYCLE closed only by a derived edge stays BLOCK.
